variants.direction: L20 — RAKED AFT SHELL. Build a compact fuselage that swells behind the narrow cockpit coupling and then tapers inward before the propulsion block; its side profile is a low rising arc interpreted as 3–4 broad crisp facets, NOT a rectangular slab. Its cargo roof is a calm central plateau. Behind that roof, a single BROAD TRANSVERSE RAKED PLATE rises directly from the solid engine collar, leaning backward at about 55 degrees. Seen from the side this is an angled wedge-like aft wall; seen from the rear it is a wide flattened trapezoid with a shallow central relief. It is a load-bearing aft shell/deflector concept, rooted along its entire bottom edge, NOT an elevated spoiler on legs and not a vertical dorsal sail. Keep it modest in height, inside roughly original ship height. There is no open arch or horizontal bridge under it. Two differently sized engines remain one above the other, exposed below this shell in short separate mounts. Three moving wing leaves per side have asymmetric broad trapezoidal outlines and a clipped angular fan edge; the upper root blend grows from the lower hull shoulder, not an attached rectangular ledge. Neck uses a short slim stepped coupling behind the UNCHANGED cockpit instead of three giant armor rings. The big design gesture is rounded/faceted forward mass pinched into a backward-raked stern. Label L20.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Design an original alternate hull architecture for a PIRATE LIBERTY ELITE FIGHTER in Freelancer, using the attached original references. This is a serious exploration of primary form and structural relationships. The design must be identifiable at silhouette level, not a familiar box with a different recess.

REFERENCES:
Image 1: immutable native cockpit. Reproduce its EXACT long low rounded glazed capsule shell, thin glazing frames, large curved side panes, long central top pane, small rear side panes, blunt glazed nose and original proportions. The cabin itself forms the nose. Its shell and windows are not redesign territory. Neck geometry BEHIND this cabin may change.
Images 2 and 3: historical Liberty industrial design language. Use changing cross-sections, directed broad planes, fan motifs, controlled curved-to-faceted transitions, and an integrated mechanical core. Their cabins differ from ours: NEVER copy those cabins. These are a vocabulary, not layouts to trace.
Image 4: actual wing motion ONLY. Each side has THREE broad overlapping rigid leaves, connected through compact sequential pivots near the forward root. Whole leaves fan outward and rotate backward to nest along the hull. Do not copy the original fixed body or its pink rear piece from this mechanics image. Three leaves are not three stationary adjacent fingers.
Image 5: the native paired cargo roof doors. TWO LONG NARROW DOORS SIDE BY SIDE, longitudinal center seam, outer longitudinal hinges, opening sideways/up. Keep a central clear cargo opening and room for their sweep.

Develop the exact architecture below. Preserve the cockpit and a plausible volume for cargo; retain three-leaf folding wings with real layered thickness and a clear forward root. The silhouette needs native-level height and volume, not a flattened fighter jet. Rough pirate repair comes through functional remade joins, angular replacement skin and a few exposed solid mechanical seats; do not cover the ship in junk. Give medium geometric detail where components meet, large calm skin surfaces elsewhere. Avoid exposed pipes, rod frameworks, stacked architectural ornament, tiny rivets, spikes and skulls.
A car-style rear wing on two legs is expressly excluded. Treat the aft fixed structure as a ship component whose shape is specified below. No generic raised horizontal bar with downturned ends. Do not force every variant to share the same long box hull, three thick neck rings, large bordered side recess, identical fan-tip silhouette or engine housing. No ornamental edge frames. The new geometry must connect convincingly, rather than decorating an unchanged fuselage.

Render a refined industrial design concept with clear linework and restrained solid shading, subtly textured grey metal with limited ivory repaired panels and local rust-red patches. Do not make a red tailbar and red middle wing the repeated color formula. Show a compact fighter, never a transport. Warm neutral background, no environment.
Landscape sheet: LARGE side-biased three-quarter view, nose LEFT, little foreshortening. Smaller true SIDE, TOP with nose UP, REAR three-quarter and TOP STOWED views. All depict the SAME design. Clearly show the new aft structure and hull cross-section. The STOWED inset must keep full-size leaves folded backward, not remove or scale them. Top cargo seam vertical. Text only the concept code and SIDE, TOP, REAR, STOWED.

ARCHITECTURE:

Build a compact fuselage that swells behind the narrow cockpit coupling and then tapers inward before the propulsion block; its side profile is a low rising arc interpreted as 3–4 broad crisp facets, NOT a rectangular slab. Keep it modest in height, inside roughly original ship height. There is no open arch or horizontal bridge under it. Two differently sized engines remain one above the other, exposed below this shell in short separate mounts. Three moving wing leaves per side have asymmetric broad trapezoidal outlines and a clipped angular fan edge; the upper root blend grows from the lower hull shoulder, not an attached rectangular ledge. Label L20.
variants.visual_review: Наклонная кормовая пластина растёт из узла двигателей без стоек; кабина ближе к исходной, хотя совпадение геометрии не доказано. Корпус сохраняет преимущественно продольную массу. Исправлены два верхних вида: нижний двигатель скрыт под верхним, ложная боковая пара удалена.

variants.direction: L21 — SPLIT AFT FLANKS. Use a deep compact diamond-section central body, fuller BELOW the cabin centerline, with a narrower clear cargo roof above. Large angular side surfaces run diagonally backward from the front wing roots and become TWO separated broad aft cheek-planes, one on each rear flank. These solid plates are nearly vertical but lean slightly outward, their blunt swept upper edges ending below a modest original-height envelope. Each cheek attaches along a substantial length of hull skin. Their upper ends are NEVER connected by a horizontal bar. The center above the two vertically stacked engines remains open to the sky. This paired flank architecture replaces the transverse aft piece. No horns: ends are broad clipped industrial planes, not pointed demon ears. The two engines sit in a stepped central saddle BETWEEN the cheeks, upper short/wide, lower slim/long, and are individually visible. Body side outline changes into a forked stern through connected skin, not a perimeter frame or exposed rods. Three broad fan leaves per side have alternating long and short straight trailing cuts and substantial overlap; in stow they nest under the outer flanks with visible clearance. Keep the unchanged capsule cockpit well forward on a slim coupling; neck flange rhythm may merge into the root shoulder. This design's height comes from a deep belly and separated aft cheeks, while its top silhouette is a fork, not a capped rectangle. Label L21.

variants.visual_review: Две крупные раздельные кормовые щеки, открытый центр сверху и глубокое тело дают иной силуэт. Нет автомобильной перекладины. Кормовые плоскости получились массивными: это художественный риск кандидата, а не принятая форма. Точность стекла, суставов и малых видов не подтверждена.

variants.direction: L22 — LATERAL PROPULSION ARCHITECTURE. Explore a genuine alternate engine arrangement: exactly TWO compact engine nacelles mounted LEFT and RIGHT of the aft central body, rather than stacked. Keep their total width much less than deployed wing span, so this remains a fighter. The central fuselage is a deep narrow faceted keel growing from the unchanged capsule cockpit into a clear upper cargo deck; neck transition has thin transverse steps flowing into hull facets, not huge free-standing rings. Behind the cargo doors, a short SOLID TRANSVERSE STRUCTURAL BULKHEAD at hull level connects this keel to the two engine roots. This load-bearing body junction replaces the visible raised aft piece: there is NO high horizontal bar, no car spoiler, no roof bridge on struts. The upper aft contour descends directly into the nacelle shoulders, while the keel continues briefly between and below them. In TOP, body and engine roots form a broad compact Y-shaped mass distribution. Each nacelle has a polygonal body, exposed aft nozzle and a deep inner clearance cut; use compact solid supports, not beams in a cage. Three broad forward-rooted fan leaves fold backward beneath the nacelles; give those leaves long angular chisel contours with overlapping inner boundaries. The engine roots must stay clear of this folded package. Calm hull skin, two decisive concave transitions around the engine roots, restrained mismatched repair panels. This is a major alternative arrangement; the primary silhouette must clearly differ from the raked-shell or split-cheek forms. Label L22.

variants.visual_review: Два двигателя разнесены по сторонам и соединены с глубоким центральным телом; поднятой поперечной перекладины нет. Заметно иной верхний и кормовой силуэт. Нужны новые посадки/HP двигателей, если выбран. В боковой проекции корпус выглядит ниже, чем в перспективе; точные пропорции и стекло по арту не подтверждены.

user_direction: Предыдущие варианты слишком одинаковы; спойлер ошибочно трактовался как автомобильная деталь. Нужны разные конструктивные идеи и компоновки, а не вариации одной формы.
design_change: No prior generated concepts are image inputs. Source cockpit remains immutable; original wing/baydoor motion is a constraint. Neck, fixed aft form and engine mounting are design variables; L22 proposes lateral engines.
scope: Three offline raster architecture studies, not selection or production validation.

parameters.quality_steps: Built-in tool does not expose numerical quality/step controls.
